leadText: Pokémon—Zoroark: Master of Illusions (Japanese: ポケットモンスター　ダイヤモンド＆パール　 の 　ゾロアーク Pocket Monsters Diamond & Pearl the Movie - Supreme Ruler of Illusions: Zoroark) is the fourth and final Pokémon the Series: Diamond and Pearl movie and the thirteenth Pokémon movie overall. It premiered in Japanese theaters on July 10, 2010, and in in select theaters and on on February 5, 2011. In , it premiered on February 26, 2011 on the channel. The premiere was shown on YTV on March 12, 2011. It was released on Blu-ray and DVD in on June 1, 2011, and was released on DVD in the UK on August 29, 2011 and in the US on September 20, 2011. On September 17, 2011 and September 18, 2011, it was available on Pokémon.com.
plainText:
Pokémon—Zoroark: Master of Illusions (Japanese: ポケットモンスター　ダイヤモンド＆パール　 の 　ゾロアーク Pocket Monsters Diamond & Pearl the Movie - Supreme Ruler of Illusions: Zoroark) is the fourth and final Pokémon the Series: Diamond and Pearl movie and the thirteenth Pokémon movie overall. It premiered in Japanese theaters on July 10, 2010, and in in select theaters and on on February 5, 2011. In , it premiered on February 26, 2011 on the channel. The premiere was shown on YTV on March 12, 2011. It was released on Blu-ray and DVD in on June 1, 2011, and was released on DVD in the UK on August 29, 2011 and in the US on September 20, 2011. On September 17, 2011 and September 18, 2011, it was available on Pokémon.com.

==Blurb==
 
 The Fury of Zoroark Has Been Unleashed!

The Pokémon Baccer World Cup.

It is the most anticipated event of the year, and as hundreds flock to Crown City to watch the exciting competition unfold, Ash, Pikachu, and his friends encounter a mysterious new Pokémon they have never seen before.

But when the three Legendary Pokémon Raikou, Entei, and Suicune suddenly arrive and begin rampaging through the streets, it’s up to Ash and his companions, along with their new Pokémon friend Zorua, to uncover the secret behind the immense and powerful forces at work.

What strange and dangerous powers are afoot in Crown City? Why did Celebi suddenly return after vanishing for twenty years? And why is the mighty Zoroark unleashing its fury upon the town? The quest for these answers leads down an uncertain path filled with peril—can Ash and his companions find enough courage, strength, and friendship to unearth the mystery in time to save Crown City? 

==Plot==
 and stop at a Pokémon Center where they watch a Pokémon Baccer exhibition match between the and evolutionary lines. , disguised as janitors, ask about the game, and and explain the Pokémon Baccer World Cup. The broadcast then highlights the "Nimbasa Legends", a popular team consisting of the Legendary beasts, led by businessman Grings Kodai. A clip of the Legendary Pokémon in action excites everyone for the World Cup. Ash is eager to reach Crown City, the location of the big game, before the day's end. Brock assures the group that he can find a shortcut.

 
Elsewhere, a rests in a massive airship as a sleepy climbs out of its fur. Suddenly, the wall opens, revealing the Legendary beasts. Zorua attempts to leap towards them but is swiftly placed back in Zoroark's mane. Grings Kodai and his assistant Rowena observe from a high window in a separate room. Kodai tests Zoroark's s by showing it holograms of the Legendary Pokémon and training it to mimic them and their moves. He also activates an illusion canceler in his bracelet. Transformed as , Zoroark unleashes thunderclouds that penetrate the walls, startling Rowena, despite her illusion canceler also being active. Kodai is impressed with Zoroark's illusions, noting that they even show up on camera.

Kodai's bodyguard, Goone, announces their imminent arrival in Crown City. The holograms of the Legendary beasts deactivate, and Zoroark reverts to its true form. Zorua jumps out of Zoroark's fur and looks around, but seizes Zorua while Zoroark is restrained by a harmful red energy beam. Kodai threatens to harm Zorua if Zoroark disobeys him. Unbeknownst to Zoroark, Zorua escapes from Ninjask and eludes one of Goone's by mimicking its form, confusing it long enough for Zorua to slip through a small hole. Zorua then breaks through a panel and falls out of the airship. During the fall, Zorua grabs a Skiploom's blooms, and transforms into one to float safely to the ground. Inside the airship, Goone confirms to Kodai that Zorua has escaped, but Kodai is not discouraged, as Goone still has Zorua's visual data. As midnight approaches, Kodai notes that he has one day to find the Time Ripple before it disappears. Right on cue, a Time Ripple opens in Crown City, and the Mythical Pokémon emerges just before midnight, after which the rift fades.

 
As Ash and Dawn follow Brock on a shortcut to Crown City, the group realizes they are lost. Meanwhile, Zorua, still disguised as a Skiploom, bumps into Team Rocket on their pedal-powered balloon. They are heading towards Crown City to steal the Legendary beasts, but Zorua nearly knocks them off before falling onto an angry . Zorua reverts to its true form, giggles, and dodges a group of Vigoroth before realizing it's headed toward a cliff. senses the commotion and alerts Ash and his friends, who see Zorua at the cliff's edge, pursued by the Vigoroth. They then witness Zorua transform into a Vigoroth and change back. As Zorua begins to slip, Ash and Dawn send out and , and everyone scolds the Vigoroth for ganging up on Zorua, causing the Vigoroth to retreat. Zorua insists that it didn't need any help. Ash and his friends begin to argue, before realizing that Zorua just . They are amazed to meet such a strange new Pokémon. Zorua reveals that it's headed to Crown City to save its "Meema", explaining that its Meema was captured trying to protect it. As they head toward the city, Zorua shares how it and Zoroark were abducted from their home across the sea. and Pikachu convince Ash and his friends to help Zorua, who, after accepting them as its new friends, stuns them by transforming into Ash. Pikachu then reverts Zorua back by grabbing its still-visible tail, prompting Zorua to transform into Pikachu.

With Zorua gone, Kodai resorts to using live video of a hologram showing a scared Zorua to compel Zoroark to create illusions of the Legendary beasts attacking Crown City. Goone then informs Kodai that remote camera drones have been dispatched to capture footage of the illusions. That morning, Celebi flies around Crown City, greeting the wild Pokémon. A woman named notices Celebi as it flies by and causes the flowers she was watering to bloom. Tammy rushes to tell her friend , and they tearfully recall Celebi's last visit twenty years ago. They are overjoyed that the city's trees and flowers are finally well enough for Celebi to return. As the morning bell tolls, Team Rocket wakes up in a tree where their balloon crashed and laments their interrupted sleep. They notice Zoroark leap from a building and use before transforming into to create floods, to form a conflagration, and Raikou to unleash a thunderstorm. As this happens, Kodai manipulates the footage to make it seem as though Zoroark has taken control of the Legendary beasts and unleashed them on Crown City, editing the video to depict damage to a statue and a bus stop. Sensing danger, the real Legendary beasts, the guardians of Crown City, begin making their way to defend the city.

 
Everyone sheltering in the flower shop except Tammy and Joe evacuates the old town in Crown City, and Officer Jenny announces that no one will be allowed back in until the situation is under control. Ash and his friends arrive, and after Jenny and Peg explain what they saw, a broadcast from Kodai appears on a nearby monitor. In the broadcast, Kodai asserts Zoroark to be an evil and dangerous Pokémon, and that the city is off limits until it is recaptured. After seeing Zoroark on the screen, Zorua identifies the Pokémon as its "Meema" and takes the form of Brock before running off. As Zorua explains that Kodai is the real villain, a journalist named Karl appears wanting to know more. Brock tries to suggest that Zorua is actually his crazy twin brother, but Karl isn't convinced and grabs Zorua's tail, causing Zorua to change back. Karl recognizes as the pre-evolved form of , and is amazed that it can talk. 

As Kodai and Rowena spot Celebi with their camera drones, Kodai suddenly has several . He sees the Time Ripple and a nearby countdown clock, and then Ash, his friends, Karl, and Rowena trying to stop him, and then sees himself absorbing the power of the Time Ripple. Kodai worries that his ability to see the future has become clouded. 

Karl decides to help Ash and his friends bring Zorua to Zoroark by taking them through the underground sewers back to the old part of the city. In the sewers, Karl has his use to light the way. As they walk, Karl explains that Grings Kodai has been called "the man who can see into the future" due to his string of business successes, including having acquired control over the mainstream media.

Kodai next orders Goone to recapture Zoroark. After being lured in by another hologram of Zorua, Zoroark is trapped by a drone, which then transforms into an electrified cage. Goone then transports Zoroark back to the airship. After Ash and the others emerge from the sewers, Zorua catches Zoroark's scent. Karl notices that the nearby bus stop is completely unharmed, despite what was broadcasted, and realizes that the footage was manipulated by Kodai, and that the Legendary beasts were actually illusions created by Zoroark. Remembering his visions, Kodai rides across the town on his hoverboard checking each countdown clock to find the one where the Time Ripple is located. He is then alerted to the presence of Ash, and once again deploys Goone. While following Zoroark's scent, Ash and the others stumble upon a statue of the Legendary beasts, regarded as the guardian protectors of Crown City. Karl notices that the statue is also in one piece despite the broadcasts. 

 
Zorua runs off to look for Zoroark and stops to slash a monitor displaying Kodai, which scares the nearby wild Pokémon. Zorua is then stopped by Joe's and lulled to sleep by Tammy's and its . When Ash and the others catch up to Zorua, Mightyena tackles Karl and licks him. The group then meets up with Tammy and Joe, the latter of which is revealed to be Karl's grandfather. Tammy and Joe learn the truth about Kodai's ruse, and they tell the others about the return of Celebi. 

 
On the airship, Zoroark grows frustrated as it struggles to break free from its cage and lets out a vicious roar. Sensing its mother, Zorua wakes from its slumber, runs outside, and slips through the small gaps of a fence. Ash, his friends, and Karl run after it but are stopped by the fence. Ash and Dawn instruct Pikachu and Piplup to follow Zorua through the fence, and Karl leads the rest of the group to the other side.

A wild 's stops Zorua in its tracks. Zorua is then surrounded by the agitated wild Pokémon. Pikachu and Piplup arrive and try to convince the Pokémon to calm down. Despite this, uses , which Pikachu deflects with . Piplup and Bellsprout argue, but Bellsprout knocks Piplup back towards Zorua and Pikachu. The other wild Pokémon then close in around the three of them. Before a fight can break out, Celebi flies in and greets everyone while turning all of the nearby flowers into . Ash and the others run by, still outside the fenced-in nature area, and notice the Berries forming and watch as the wild Pokémon happily eat the Berries and share them with Pikachu and Piplup. Celebi then grabs a Pecha Berry and gives it to Zorua, which it eats before giggling and changing into Celebi. Celebi is surprised and tries to fly with Zorua, but Zorua explains that it can't fly and changes back. Zorua befriends Celebi and asks it to help find Zoroark, and takes off as Celebi, Pikachu, and Piplup follow it out of the garden.

Ash and the others notice Celebi running off with the other Pokémon, and start to give chase, but find themselves surrounded by Goone's Pokémon and then caged by another one of Kodai's drones. Kodai appears on his hoverboard and confirms to Ash and the others that he can see the future, including the obstacles in his way, and asserts that all obstacles will be removed. The panels then close around the cage and Goone takes it back to the airship. Meanwhile, Celebi helps Zorua up a massive tree just outside the old part of the city, and Pikachu and Piplup follow. On a high-up branch, Zorua howls for its mother. Zoroark senses this and continues attacking the sides of the cage. Zorua becomes despondent and runs into a hole in the tree, but Celebi flies over and uses its powers to make a comforting nest for Zorua, which reminds it of its mother's fur and soothes it to sleep.

Rowena is looking through Kodai's computer and finds that his most important files are locked behind a password, which she easily guesses. Amongst the files, Rowena finds various images and text about Celebi, the Time Ripple, and Kodai's gadgets, such as his extending robotic arm. Rowena is then startled by a call from Goone instructing her to stay put. She then sees live video of the cage holding Ash and the others and decides to investigate. She introduces herself to Ash and the others as Kodai's executive secretary, but Karl recognizes her as a fellow investigative journalist. Rowena reveals that she is working undercover and has the complete files of everything she's learned about Kodai and his plans. She and the others then take a boat back into the city. On the way, she explains Kodai's plans to absorb the energy of the Time Ripple to rejuvenate his future visions. She explains that twenty years ago, Kodai received his powers by absorbing the energy of the Time Ripple with the claw of his robotic arm, but the flow of time energy reversed and caused all of the trees and flowers in the city to wither and die.

Kodai checks the final countdown clock for the Time Ripple on his map, but does not find it. However, a vision indicates to him that he needs to go after Celebi itself. As Zorua and the other Pokémon make their way down the big tree, Celebi is spotted by one of Kodai's drones. Kodai arrives on his hoverboard and tries to take Celebi using 's , but Shuppet is stopped by Pikachu's . Three of Goone's Ninjask then attack Pikachu and Piplup using , causing Pikachu to cling onto the tree's branch with Piplup hanging on by Pikachu's tail. Zorua changes into Tangrowth and creates illusions of vines to hold back Shuppet and , but Kodai cancels the illusions with his bracelet and instructs Shuppet to use Shadow Ball. Zorua takes the hit and collapses while calling out for its mother. Zoroark, sensing its child's pain, finally musters enough strength to break out of its cage. Just then, the real Legendary beasts arrive in Crown City and are spotted by Tammy and Joe. Zoroark uses Night Daze to break out of its holding room and then leaps, bursting out the top of the airship. Back at the tree, Kodai grabs Celebi and once again sees a vision of himself absorbing the power of the Time Ripple. Kodai shakes Celebi, demanding to show him more. Celebi screams in pain and, elsewhere, the Time Ripple reveals itself once again. Zorua jumps on Kodai's head causing him to lose control of his hoverboard and crash. Kodai then furiously throws Zorua off his head and onto the ground.

 
On top of the airship, Zoroark is confronted by the real Legendary beasts, who are convinced that Zoroark is a threat to the city. The Legendary Pokémon all attack, causing the airship to explode. Zoroark emerges from the water before blocking and dodging more attacks from the Legendary beasts. Back at the tree, Pikachu manages to pull itself back up along with Piplup. At the bottom of the tree, Kodai once again tries to grab Celebi, but Pikachu and Piplup stop him with a Thunderbolt and , respectively. Goone calls on two of his Scizor, who send Pikachu and Piplup flying off the tree. However, they are saved by Dawn's Togekiss as Ash and the others arrive, including Rowena, as previously foreseen by Kodai. Pikachu forces Kodai and Goone away from Celebi and Zorua with Thunderbolt as Ash and Dawn run in to retrieve them, and Piplup uses Bubble Beam to hold back Goone's Ninjask, allowing Ash and the others to escape. Goone's other Pokémon begin to pursue but are blocked by the wild Pokémon and their Bullet Seed. Ash and the others drive by on a motorboat and Pikachu destroys a camera drone with Thunderbolt as they head off down the river. Kodai then sends a small pen-sized spy drone to follow them. Meanwhile, Zoroark's battle with the three Legendary beasts gradually makes its way through the city.

 
Ash and the others arrive at Joe's workshop and reunite with Tammy and Joe, who are both surprised to see Celebi again. Tammy and Joe are brought up to speed as Brock wraps Celebi's injured arm, while Zorua laments that it could not protect Celebi. Tammy and Joe reveal that they saw the Legendary beasts earlier, and that the Legendary Pokémon believe Zoroark is the real danger to Crown City. Zorua, worried for its mother, leaps for the door. Celebi attempts to follow it, but struggles to fly due to its injuries. Rowena assures that Celebi will be fine if they can get it to the Time Ripple, and explains that Kodai was looking for it by the countdown clocks, but has already searched them with no success. However, Joe reveals that he is the one who designed the countdown clocks and knows that there is one more in the Pokémon Baccer World Cup stadium. Pikachu hears the spy drone as it begins to take off, and destroys it with Thunderbolt. Rowena identifies the drone as Kodai's, which alerts everyone to the fact that Kodai has heard everything they've said, so the group resolves to get Celebi to the stadium first. Brock leads the group through a shortcut in the sewers with the help of Bronzor, certain that this time his shortcut won't get them lost.

Zoroark finds itself surrounded by the Legendary beasts and uses its illusions to trap them in clusters of crystals. Karl and the others arrive and Rowena reveals the illusions with her canceler. Joe scolds Zoroark, and Tammy shouts at Zoroark that the Legendary Pokémon have merely made a mistake. Joe's Mightyena then destroys the illusions. Mightyena, Tangrowth, and the wild Pokémon put themselves between Zoroark and the Legendary beasts, quelling the fight. Meanwhile, Ash and his friends emerge near the stadium before spotting Kodai and Goone. Ash continues to the stadium with Celebi and Bronzor, while Dawn sends out Mamoswine and Brock sends out Croagunk and . Goone is left to deal with Brock and Dawn while Kodai heads for the stadium. As Kodai approaches from behind, Ash tells Pikachu to use Thunderbolt while Kodai has Mismagius block it with . Ash then sends Celebi to fly to the Time Ripple with Bronzor as Kodai pursues them into the stadium. 

During Goone's battle with Brock and Dawn, Zoroark rushes in and knocks Goone and his Pokémon out with a slew of attacks. In the stadium, Shuppet uses Thunderbolt on Celebi, revealing it to be Zorua flying with the aid of Bronzor's Psychic to help it fly. Karl's Bronzor uses Psychic to throw aside Kodai's vehicle, but Kodai's Pokémon knock Bronzor down. Zorua then leaps and bites Kodai's arm. He angrily throws Zorua off and grabs it with his robotic claw, causing Zorua to cry out. Zoroark senses Zorua and starts toward the stadium. Inside the entrance to the stadium, Ash lets the real Celebi out of his backpack and starts searching for the Time Ripple. They spot it, but as they run toward it, Mismagius stops them with Psychic. Kodai begins to walk toward the Time Ripple, but Zoroark leaps down from above. Zoroark charges towards Kodai, but stops after he threatens to kill Zorua. He then shocks Zorua with his robotic arm and orders Shuppet to finish off Zoroark. Kodai approaches the Time Ripple and starts absorbing its power, unconcerned that the city's trees and flowers will wither and die again. 

 
As the events of twenty years ago start to repeat themselves, Ash yells at Kodai to stop, knowing the plants would die. Kodai doesn't care in the slightest and confesses that he was responsible back then as well, but brags that no one will ever know what he's done, with Zoroark to take all the blame. As Kodai gloats over his apparent victory, Zoroark smirks, and time appears to start reversing. Kodai is baffled at how this could have been an illusion, until he realizes that Zorua had destroyed his illusion canceler when it bit his arm earlier. Karl and Rowena then reveal that they have captured Kodai's confession on tape. Kodai starts backing up while Zorua manages to start making its way towards its mother. As Zorua and Zoroark draw closer to each other, Kodai orders Shuppet to use Shadow Ball on Zorua, but Zoroark leaps to take the attack instead. Kodai then grabs Zoroark with his robotic arm and begins to shock the Pokémon, furious at the deception. However, Zoroark breaks free with , destroying the robotic arm and knocking Kodai and Shuppet back in the process. Dawn and Brock arrive as Piplup knocks Mismagius back with Bubble Beam, freeing Ash and Celebi from Psychic. Mismagius attempts to attack Ash and Celebi with Psywave, but is blocked by Bronzor's . Pikachu then defeats Mismagius with Thunderbolt and before Zoroark defeats Shuppet with another Dark Pulse. Kodai staggers backwards and tries to go for the Time Ripple when the Legendary beasts appear, prompting Kodai to make a run for it. Just then, Zoroark collapses.

 
While Kodai is running away, Zoroark creates an illusion to make him think that he is safe atop his plane, high in the air. However, she quickly cancels the illusion, causing Kodai to fall off the platform he was on and pass out in the stadium field. Zoroark then closes its eyes with a satisfied smile. In tears, Zorua pleads and cries for Zoroark to wake up, creating an illusion of a beautiful grassy field around them—their home. Celebi reaches for the Time Ripple, and Ash brings Celebi closer to it. Celebi then uses the power of the Time Ripple to heal itself and Zoroark. As Zoroark recovers and embraces with Zorua in a tearful reunion. Zorua turns and thanks everyone for helping saving its mother. Celebi smiles and then time travels away in billows of light as it makes the surrounding greenery bloom.

As Kodai regains consciousness, he awakens to witness his confession being broadcast all over the news and finds himself surrounded by the entire town, including Officer Jenny waiting to arrest him for his crimes. Later, Zoroark and Zorua board a ship heading back to their home with Karl and Rowena. Before they depart, Zorua mischievously takes on the form of Ash before being turned back to its original form when Rowena grabs its tail. Zoroark is likewise in the form of Pikachu before transforming back to its true form after its child is revealed. As the ship sets sail, Ash yells out a promise to Zorua that they will come visit Zorua and Zoroark in their region next.

Later, Ash and his friends cheer and watch the events of the Pokémon Baccer World Cup from the stands. Kodai and Goone are sent to prison for their crimes as the news spreads across the world. The Legendary beasts look on at the ship carrying Zorua and Zoroark, bidding their farewells to the before going their separate ways. Zoroark and Zorua nuzzle each other affectionately as the ship approaches a mist-covered island.

==Events==
 
===Pre-order distribution===
In Japan, people who pre-ordered tickets to the movie received a Legendary beast; Entei, Raikou or Suicune. In North America, these were distributed at GameStop stores, with a certain amount of time allotted for each of the three Pokémon. They were also later distributed via Wi-Fi for European language games and locally in . The Shiny Legendary beasts allow players to encounter at the Lostlorn Forest when migrated into a Generation V game.

===Movie distribution===
A Celebi could also be downloaded in the cinema when the film was showing in theaters. In addition, Celebi was distributed at GameStop stores at the Pokémon Black and White Sampling Tour and other GameStop stores soon afterward. These Celebi allow players to befriend at Castelia City.

===Other distributions===
Goone's Scizor was made available to Japanese and Korean versions of the Generation IV games via Wi-Fi.

Those who attended the Black and White Tour in the United States and obtained tickets to the movie could turn in their ticket stubs later on to receive an Pokémon TCG card featuring .

==Trivia==
This was released between DP183 and DP184 in Japan. However, it chronologically takes place sometime before the aforementioned episodes, as they are placed in the middle of the Lily of the Valley Conference.
This is the only Pokémon the Series: Diamond and Pearl movie that is a standalone movie. The other three Diamond & Pearl movies are part of a trilogy. As such, it is the only Diamond & Pearl movie not to star a member of the Pokémon of myth.
The movie's fictitious setting is based on various locations in and , such as , , , and .
This movie marks the first time all three of the Legendary beasts appear at the same time in the , and also the first time receives a starring role in a movie.
This movie also marks the first time a Legendary Pokémon (in this case, Raikou, Entei, and Suicune) appears in the .
This is the third movie so far that does not have a Legendary Pokémon as the main featured Pokémon, the first being Spell of the Unown: Entei and the second being Lucario and the Mystery of Mew.
This movie ends with Team Rocket being the last characters to appear before the ending credits. This is a pattern found in early movies, which stopped occurring after Celebi: The Voice of the Forest, and has not happened again.
The teaser trailer shown at the end of Arceus and the Jewel of Life showed and locked in an aerial battle, while a later trailer showed a strange city and Ash meeting a darker version of himself. None of these elements made it into the final movie.
This movie was released in Taiwan on July 30, 2010, which was just 20 days after its Japanese premiere.
Professor Rowan, , Johanna, Paul, Zoey, , Nando, , Conway, Ursula, and Palmer make cameo appearances in the movie's credits, along with the Sinnoh Gym Leaders battled and Elite Four. Most of them appear with one of their Pokémon.
makes a cameo in the beginning of the movie with a , seen in with Ash.
This makes this movie the second in which Ash battles a Trainer with a Donphan in the beginning. The first was in Mewtwo Strikes Back.
The Officer Jenny seen in this movie has a star symbol on her hat, which was the same symbol worn by the Jenny in Viridian City (who was also the first Officer Jenny to appear in the animated series).
This is the only animated series appearance of a Generation V Pokémon prior to Pokémon the Series: Black & White.
When Team Rocket sees Zoroark, Jessie asks "Who's that Pokémon?". While this is obviously a reference to the feature of the same name in the TV show, it may also be a premonition that it would return to the show starting with the next season.
During the scene where flies around the city, when it calms the feuding Pokémon, and when it revives Zoroark, remade versions of the Voice of the Forest melody from Celebi: The Voice of the Forest can be heard.
The movie was shown at local theaters during the Pokémon Black Version and White Version Tour between February 5, 2011 and March 20, 2011 in .
This makes it the first movie shown in U.S. theaters since Pokémon Heroes: Latios & Latias in 2003.
In the initial Cartoon Network broadcasts, the entire prologue was cut, with the movie beginning immediately at the title sequence. These scenes are present in the theatrical version.
This cut was made by Cartoon Network The Pokémon Company International's permission, and was restored in future airings as of February 16, 2011.
As of this movie, Ash has seen all the Legendary Pokémon from the first four generations at least once.
Karl's cap has a picture of a on it; that Pokémon had only been officially revealed four days prior to this movie's release.
During the Pokémon Baccer match, the announcer titles Kodai's team as the Nimbasa Legends. Nimbasa City is a city that appears in Generation V, hinting to Kodai's possible origins.
During the title sequence, after Zoroark: Master of Illusions is displayed, a part of the music from Lostlorn Forest can be heard.
This movie marks the debut of the made-up writing system created for the animated series, which would start being used consistently from Pokémon the Series: Black & White onward.
This movie marks the first animated series appearance of a other than the one that belonged to Morrison.

===Errors===
 
 
In the credits, Palmer's 's mouth was the same color as its horn and the top-most part of its body.
As Ash asks "What do you mean?" in the scene when Ash and his friends were trapped in the cage by Kodai, Dawn's hair clip is the same color as her hair.
During Kodai's "apology" broadcast, Peg can be briefly seen standing with Ash and his friends. Her eyes are drawn oval-shaped, with visible pupils, as opposed to all of the other times in the movie when she is drawn without pupils. 
Among the Pokémon using is , a Pokémon unable to legally learn the move.
Whether Zorua's illusions allow it to use the natural abilities of the Pokémon its disguised as is inconsistent. Early in the film, Zorua is able to float down safely from a dangerous height while taking the form of . Despite this, it is shown later in the movie that Zorua cannot fly as .
Near the end of the movie, while Kodai is pursuing and (disguised as Celebi), his illusion canceler failed to reveal Zorua's disguise even though it was not yet broken at that point.
Karl's uses to deflect a from which should not have worked as Psywave is a special move and Reflect only affects physical moves.

===Dub edits===
Zorua calls Zoroark "Meema" instead of "Maa".
In the original version, the password to Kodai's secret files was "Time Ripple". In the English dub it is "V-I-S-I-O-N". This is likely due to "Time Ripple" having 6 characters in Japanese kana but 11 letters in English.
During the climax of the movie in Japanese, Zorua says "Maa... I couldn't do anything", while in the English dub, he instead says the much darker phrase of "I guess there isn't much time left for me..." implying that he expects to die.
While Zorua is in Tangrowth's arm after being hit by Sleep Powder, he mumbles "I'm not sleepy...!" in Japanese, while in English he remains silent.
Ice Cream Syndrome is replaced as the ending song of the movie by a new song titled I Believe in You.
Zorua was originally told by Zoroark never to talk to humans, but in the dub, was told never to talk to strangers.

sections.heading: Lead
sections.text: Pokémon—Zoroark: Master of Illusions (Japanese: ポケットモンスター　ダイヤモンド＆パール　 の 　ゾロアーク Pocket Monsters Diamond & Pearl the Movie - Supreme Ruler of Illusions: Zoroark) is the fourth and final Pokémon the Series: Diamond and Pearl movie and the thirteenth Pokémon movie overall. It premiered in Japanese theaters on July 10, 2010, and in in select theaters and on on February 5, 2011. In , it premiered on February 26, 2011 on the channel. The premiere was shown on YTV on March 12, 2011. It was released on Blu-ray and DVD in on June 1, 2011, and was released on DVD in the UK on August 29, 2011 and in the US on September 20, 2011. On September 17, 2011 and September 18, 2011, it was available on Pokémon.com.

sections.heading: Blurb
sections.text:
The Fury of Zoroark Has Been Unleashed!

The Pokémon Baccer World Cup.

It is the most anticipated event of the year, and as hundreds flock to Crown City to watch the exciting competition unfold, Ash, Pikachu, and his friends encounter a mysterious new Pokémon they have never seen before.

But when the three Legendary Pokémon Raikou, Entei, and Suicune suddenly arrive and begin rampaging through the streets, it’s up to Ash and his companions, along with their new Pokémon friend Zorua, to uncover the secret behind the immense and powerful forces at work.

What strange and dangerous powers are afoot in Crown City? Why did Celebi suddenly return after vanishing for twenty years? And why is the mighty Zoroark unleashing its fury upon the town? The quest for these answers leads down an uncertain path filled with peril—can Ash and his companions find enough courage, strength, and friendship to unearth the mystery in time to save Crown City?

sections.heading: Plot
sections.text:
and stop at a Pokémon Center where they watch a Pokémon Baccer exhibition match between the and evolutionary lines. , disguised as janitors, ask about the game, and and explain the Pokémon Baccer World Cup. The broadcast then highlights the "Nimbasa Legends", a popular team consisting of the Legendary beasts, led by businessman Grings Kodai. A clip of the Legendary Pokémon in action excites everyone for the World Cup. Ash is eager to reach Crown City, the location of the big game, before the day's end. Brock assures the group that he can find a shortcut.

 
Elsewhere, a rests in a massive airship as a sleepy climbs out of its fur. Suddenly, the wall opens, revealing the Legendary beasts. Zorua attempts to leap towards them but is swiftly placed back in Zoroark's mane. Grings Kodai and his assistant Rowena observe from a high window in a separate room. Kodai tests Zoroark's s by showing it holograms of the Legendary Pokémon and training it to mimic them and their moves. He also activates an illusion canceler in his bracelet. Transformed as , Zoroark unleashes thunderclouds that penetrate the walls, startling Rowena, despite her illusion canceler also being active. Kodai is impressed with Zoroark's illusions, noting that they even show up on camera.

Kodai's bodyguard, Goone, announces their imminent arrival in Crown City. The holograms of the Legendary beasts deactivate, and Zoroark reverts to its true form. Zorua jumps out of Zoroark's fur and looks around, but seizes Zorua while Zoroark is restrained by a harmful red energy beam. Kodai threatens to harm Zorua if Zoroark disobeys him. Unbeknownst to Zoroark, Zorua escapes from Ninjask and eludes one of Goone's by mimicking its form, confusing it long enough for Zorua to slip through a small hole. Zorua then breaks through a panel and falls out of the airship. During the fall, Zorua grabs a Skiploom's blooms, and transforms into one to float safely to the ground. Inside the airship, Goone confirms to Kodai that Zorua has escaped, but Kodai is not discouraged, as Goone still has Zorua's visual data. As midnight approaches, Kodai notes that he has one day to find the Time Ripple before it disappears. Right on cue, a Time Ripple opens in Crown City, and the Mythical Pokémon emerges just before midnight, after which the rift fades.

 
As Ash and Dawn follow Brock on a shortcut to Crown City, the group realizes they are lost. Meanwhile, Zorua, still disguised as a Skiploom, bumps into Team Rocket on their pedal-powered balloon. They are heading towards Crown City to steal the Legendary beasts, but Zorua nearly knocks them off before falling onto an angry . Zorua reverts to its true form, giggles, and dodges a group of Vigoroth before realizing it's headed toward a cliff. senses the commotion and alerts Ash and his friends, who see Zorua at the cliff's edge, pursued by the Vigoroth. They then witness Zorua transform into a Vigoroth and change back. As Zorua begins to slip, Ash and Dawn send out and , and everyone scolds the Vigoroth for ganging up on Zorua, causing the Vigoroth to retreat. Zorua insists that it didn't need any help. Ash and his friends begin to argue, before realizing that Zorua just . They are amazed to meet such a strange new Pokémon. Zorua reveals that it's headed to Crown City to save its "Meema", explaining that its Meema was captured trying to protect it. As they head toward the city, Zorua shares how it and Zoroark were abducted from their home across the sea. and Pikachu convince Ash and his friends to help Zorua, who, after accepting them as its new friends, stuns them by transforming into Ash. Pikachu then reverts Zorua back by grabbing its still-visible tail, prompting Zorua to transform into Pikachu.

With Zorua gone, Kodai resorts to using live video of a hologram showing a scared Zorua to compel Zoroark to create illusions of the Legendary beasts attacking Crown City. Goone then informs Kodai that remote camera drones have been dispatched to capture footage of the illusions. That morning, Celebi flies around Crown City, greeting the wild Pokémon. A woman named notices Celebi as it flies by and causes the flowers she was watering to bloom. Tammy rushes to tell her friend , and they tearfully recall Celebi's last visit twenty years ago. They are overjoyed that the city's trees and flowers are finally well enough for Celebi to return. As the morning bell tolls, Team Rocket wakes up in a tree where their balloon crashed and laments their interrupted sleep. They notice Zoroark leap from a building and use before transforming into to create floods, to form a conflagration, and Raikou to unleash a thunderstorm. As this happens, Kodai manipulates the footage to make it seem as though Zoroark has taken control of the Legendary beasts and unleashed them on Crown City, editing the video to depict damage to a statue and a bus stop. Sensing danger, the real Legendary beasts, the guardians of Crown City, begin making their way to defend the city.

 
Everyone sheltering in the flower shop except Tammy and Joe evacuates the old town in Crown City, and Officer Jenny announces that no one will be allowed back in until the situation is under control. Ash and his friends arrive, and after Jenny and Peg explain what they saw, a broadcast from Kodai appears on a nearby monitor. In the broadcast, Kodai asserts Zoroark to be an evil and dangerous Pokémon, and that the city is off limits until it is recaptured. After seeing Zoroark on the screen, Zorua identifies the Pokémon as its "Meema" and takes the form of Brock before running off. As Zorua explains that Kodai is the real villain, a journalist named Karl appears wanting to know more. Brock tries to suggest that Zorua is actually his crazy twin brother, but Karl isn't convinced and grabs Zorua's tail, causing Zorua to change back. Karl recognizes as the pre-evolved form of , and is amazed that it can talk. 

As Kodai and Rowena spot Celebi with their camera drones, Kodai suddenly has several . He sees the Time Ripple and a nearby countdown clock, and then Ash, his friends, Karl, and Rowena trying to stop him, and then sees himself absorbing the power of the Time Ripple. Kodai worries that his ability to see the future has become clouded. 

Karl decides to help Ash and his friends bring Zorua to Zoroark by taking them through the underground sewers back to the old part of the city. In the sewers, Karl has his use to light the way. As they walk, Karl explains that Grings Kodai has been called "the man who can see into the future" due to his string of business successes, including having acquired control over the mainstream media.

Kodai next orders Goone to recapture Zoroark. After being lured in by another hologram of Zorua, Zoroark is trapped by a drone, which then transforms into an electrified cage. Goone then transports Zoroark back to the airship. After Ash and the others emerge from the sewers, Zorua catches Zoroark's scent. Karl notices that the nearby bus stop is completely unharmed, despite what was broadcasted, and realizes that the footage was manipulated by Kodai, and that the Legendary beasts were actually illusions created by Zoroark. Remembering his visions, Kodai rides across the town on his hoverboard checking each countdown clock to find the one where the Time Ripple is located. He is then alerted to the presence of Ash, and once again deploys Goone. While following Zoroark's scent, Ash and the others stumble upon a statue of the Legendary beasts, regarded as the guardian protectors of Crown City. Karl notices that the statue is also in one piece despite the broadcasts. 

 
Zorua runs off to look for Zoroark and stops to slash a monitor displaying Kodai, which scares the nearby wild Pokémon. Zorua is then stopped by Joe's and lulled to sleep by Tammy's and its . When Ash and the others catch up to Zorua, Mightyena tackles Karl and licks him. The group then meets up with Tammy and Joe, the latter of which is revealed to be Karl's grandfather. Tammy and Joe learn the truth about Kodai's ruse, and they tell the others about the return of Celebi. 

 
On the airship, Zoroark grows frustrated as it struggles to break free from its cage and lets out a vicious roar. Sensing its mother, Zorua wakes from its slumber, runs outside, and slips through the small gaps of a fence. Ash, his friends, and Karl run after it but are stopped by the fence. Ash and Dawn instruct Pikachu and Piplup to follow Zorua through the fence, and Karl leads the rest of the group to the other side.

A wild 's stops Zorua in its tracks. Zorua is then surrounded by the agitated wild Pokémon. Pikachu and Piplup arrive and try to convince the Pokémon to calm down. Despite this, uses , which Pikachu deflects with . Piplup and Bellsprout argue, but Bellsprout knocks Piplup back towards Zorua and Pikachu. The other wild Pokémon then close in around the three of them. Before a fight can break out, Celebi flies in and greets everyone while turning all of the nearby flowers into . Ash and the others run by, still outside the fenced-in nature area, and notice the Berries forming and watch as the wild Pokémon happily eat the Berries and share them with Pikachu and Piplup. Celebi then grabs a Pecha Berry and gives it to Zorua, which it eats before giggling and changing into Celebi. Celebi is surprised and tries to fly with Zorua, but Zorua explains that it can't fly and changes back. Zorua befriends Celebi and asks it to help find Zoroark, and takes off as Celebi, Pikachu, and Piplup follow it out of the garden.

Ash and the others notice Celebi running off with the other Pokémon, and start to give chase, but find themselves surrounded by Goone's Pokémon and then caged by another one of Kodai's drones. Kodai appears on his hoverboard and confirms to Ash and the others that he can see the future, including the obstacles in his way, and asserts that all obstacles will be removed. The panels then close around the cage and Goone takes it back to the airship. Meanwhile, Celebi helps Zorua up a massive tree just outside the old part of the city, and Pikachu and Piplup follow. On a high-up branch, Zorua howls for its mother. Zoroark senses this and continues attacking the sides of the cage. Zorua becomes despondent and runs into a hole in the tree, but Celebi flies over and uses its powers to make a comforting nest for Zorua, which reminds it of its mother's fur and soothes it to sleep.

Rowena is looking through Kodai's computer and finds that his most important files are locked behind a password, which she easily guesses. Amongst the files, Rowena finds various images and text about Celebi, the Time Ripple, and Kodai's gadgets, such as his extending robotic arm. Rowena is then startled by a call from Goone instructing her to stay put. She then sees live video of the cage holding Ash and the others and decides to investigate. She introduces herself to Ash and the others as Kodai's executive secretary, but Karl recognizes her as a fellow investigative journalist. Rowena reveals that she is working undercover and has the complete files of everything she's learned about Kodai and his plans. She and the others then take a boat back into the city. On the way, she explains Kodai's plans to absorb the energy of the Time Ripple to rejuvenate his future visions. She explains that twenty years ago, Kodai received his powers by absorbing the energy of the Time Ripple with the claw of his robotic arm, but the flow of time energy reversed and caused all of the trees and flowers in the city to wither and die.

Kodai checks the final countdown clock for the Time Ripple on his map, but does not find it. However, a vision indicates to him that he needs to go after Celebi itself. As Zorua and the other Pokémon make their way down the big tree, Celebi is spotted by one of Kodai's drones. Kodai arrives on his hoverboard and tries to take Celebi using 's , but Shuppet is stopped by Pikachu's . Three of Goone's Ninjask then attack Pikachu and Piplup using , causing Pikachu to cling onto the tree's branch with Piplup hanging on by Pikachu's tail. Zorua changes into Tangrowth and creates illusions of vines to hold back Shuppet and , but Kodai cancels the illusions with his bracelet and instructs Shuppet to use Shadow Ball. Zorua takes the hit and collapses while calling out for its mother. Zoroark, sensing its child's pain, finally musters enough strength to break out of its cage. Just then, the real Legendary beasts arrive in Crown City and are spotted by Tammy and Joe. Zoroark uses Night Daze to break out of its holding room and then leaps, bursting out the top of the airship. Back at the tree, Kodai grabs Celebi and once again sees a vision of himself absorbing the power of the Time Ripple. Kodai shakes Celebi, demanding to show him more. Celebi screams in pain and, elsewhere, the Time Ripple reveals itself once again. Zorua jumps on Kodai's head causing him to lose control of his hoverboard and crash. Kodai then furiously throws Zorua off his head and onto the ground.

 
On top of the airship, Zoroark is confronted by the real Legendary beasts, who are convinced that Zoroark is a threat to the city. The Legendary Pokémon all attack, causing the airship to explode. Zoroark emerges from the water before blocking and dodging more attacks from the Legendary beasts. Back at the tree, Pikachu manages to pull itself back up along with Piplup. At the bottom of the tree, Kodai once again tries to grab Celebi, but Pikachu and Piplup stop him with a Thunderbolt and , respectively. Goone calls on two of his Scizor, who send Pikachu and Piplup flying off the tree. However, they are saved by Dawn's Togekiss as Ash and the others arrive, including Rowena, as previously foreseen by Kodai. Pikachu forces Kodai and Goone away from Celebi and Zorua with Thunderbolt as Ash and Dawn run in to retrieve them, and Piplup uses Bubble Beam to hold back Goone's Ninjask, allowing Ash and the others to escape. Goone's other Pokémon begin to pursue but are blocked by the wild Pokémon and their Bullet Seed. Ash and the others drive by on a motorboat and Pikachu destroys a camera drone with Thunderbolt as they head off down the river. Kodai then sends a small pen-sized spy drone to follow them. Meanwhile, Zoroark's battle with the three Legendary beasts gradually makes its way through the city.

 
Ash and the others arrive at Joe's workshop and reunite with Tammy and Joe, who are both surprised to see Celebi again. Tammy and Joe are brought up to speed as Brock wraps Celebi's injured arm, while Zorua laments that it could not protect Celebi. Tammy and Joe reveal that they saw the Legendary beasts earlier, and that the Legendary Pokémon believe Zoroark is the real danger to Crown City. Zorua, worried for its mother, leaps for the door. Celebi attempts to follow it, but struggles to fly due to its injuries. Rowena assures that Celebi will be fine if they can get it to the Time Ripple, and explains that Kodai was looking for it by the countdown clocks, but has already searched them with no success. However, Joe reveals that he is the one who designed the countdown clocks and knows that there is one more in the Pokémon Baccer World Cup stadium. Pikachu hears the spy drone as it begins to take off, and destroys it with Thunderbolt. Rowena identifies the drone as Kodai's, which alerts everyone to the fact that Kodai has heard everything they've said, so the group resolves to get Celebi to the stadium first. Brock leads the group through a shortcut in the sewers with the help of Bronzor, certain that this time his shortcut won't get them lost.

Zoroark finds itself surrounded by the Legendary beasts and uses its illusions to trap them in clusters of crystals. Karl and the others arrive and Rowena reveals the illusions with her canceler. Joe scolds Zoroark, and Tammy shouts at Zoroark that the Legendary Pokémon have merely made a mistake. Joe's Mightyena then destroys the illusions. Mightyena, Tangrowth, and the wild Pokémon put themselves between Zoroark and the Legendary beasts, quelling the fight. Meanwhile, Ash and his friends emerge near the stadium before spotting Kodai and Goone. Ash continues to the stadium with Celebi and Bronzor, while Dawn sends out Mamoswine and Brock sends out Croagunk and . Goone is left to deal with Brock and Dawn while Kodai heads for the stadium. As Kodai approaches from behind, Ash tells Pikachu to use Thunderbolt while Kodai has Mismagius block it with . Ash then sends Celebi to fly to the Time Ripple with Bronzor as Kodai pursues them into the stadium. 

During Goone's battle with Brock and Dawn, Zoroark rushes in and knocks Goone and his Pokémon out with a slew of attacks. In the stadium, Shuppet uses Thunderbolt on Celebi, revealing it to be Zorua flying with the aid of Bronzor's Psychic to help it fly. Karl's Bronzor uses Psychic to throw aside Kodai's vehicle, but Kodai's Pokémon knock Bronzor down. Zorua then leaps and bites Kodai's arm. He angrily throws Zorua off and grabs it with his robotic claw, causing Zorua to cry out. Zoroark senses Zorua and starts toward the stadium. Inside the entrance to the stadium, Ash lets the real Celebi out of his backpack and starts searching for the Time Ripple. They spot it, but as they run toward it, Mismagius stops them with Psychic. Kodai begins to walk toward the Time Ripple, but Zoroark leaps down from above. Zoroark charges towards Kodai, but stops after he threatens to kill Zorua. He then shocks Zorua with his robotic arm and orders Shuppet to finish off Zoroark. Kodai approaches the Time Ripple and starts absorbing its power, unconcerned that the city's trees and flowers will wither and die again. 

 
As the events of twenty years ago start to repeat themselves, Ash yells at Kodai to stop, knowing the plants would die. Kodai doesn't care in the slightest and confesses that he was responsible back then as well, but brags that no one will ever know what he's done, with Zoroark to take all the blame. As Kodai gloats over his apparent victory, Zoroark smirks, and time appears to start reversing. Kodai is baffled at how this could have been an illusion, until he realizes that Zorua had destroyed his illusion canceler when it bit his arm earlier. Karl and Rowena then reveal that they have captured Kodai's confession on tape. Kodai starts backing up while Zorua manages to start making its way towards its mother. As Zorua and Zoroark draw closer to each other, Kodai orders Shuppet to use Shadow Ball on Zorua, but Zoroark leaps to take the attack instead. Kodai then grabs Zoroark with his robotic arm and begins to shock the Pokémon, furious at the deception. However, Zoroark breaks free with , destroying the robotic arm and knocking Kodai and Shuppet back in the process. Dawn and Brock arrive as Piplup knocks Mismagius back with Bubble Beam, freeing Ash and Celebi from Psychic. Mismagius attempts to attack Ash and Celebi with Psywave, but is blocked by Bronzor's . Pikachu then defeats Mismagius with Thunderbolt and before Zoroark defeats Shuppet with another Dark Pulse. Kodai staggers backwards and tries to go for the Time Ripple when the Legendary beasts appear, prompting Kodai to make a run for it. Just then, Zoroark collapses.

 
While Kodai is running away, Zoroark creates an illusion to make him think that he is safe atop his plane, high in the air. However, she quickly cancels the illusion, causing Kodai to fall off the platform he was on and pass out in the stadium field. Zoroark then closes its eyes with a satisfied smile. In tears, Zorua pleads and cries for Zoroark to wake up, creating an illusion of a beautiful grassy field around them—their home. Celebi reaches for the Time Ripple, and Ash brings Celebi closer to it. Celebi then uses the power of the Time Ripple to heal itself and Zoroark. As Zoroark recovers and embraces with Zorua in a tearful reunion. Zorua turns and thanks everyone for helping saving its mother. Celebi smiles and then time travels away in billows of light as it makes the surrounding greenery bloom.

As Kodai regains consciousness, he awakens to witness his confession being broadcast all over the news and finds himself surrounded by the entire town, including Officer Jenny waiting to arrest him for his crimes. Later, Zoroark and Zorua board a ship heading back to their home with Karl and Rowena. Before they depart, Zorua mischievously takes on the form of Ash before being turned back to its original form when Rowena grabs its tail. Zoroark is likewise in the form of Pikachu before transforming back to its true form after its child is revealed. As the ship sets sail, Ash yells out a promise to Zorua that they will come visit Zorua and Zoroark in their region next.

Later, Ash and his friends cheer and watch the events of the Pokémon Baccer World Cup from the stands. Kodai and Goone are sent to prison for their crimes as the news spreads across the world. The Legendary beasts look on at the ship carrying Zorua and Zoroark, bidding their farewells to the before going their separate ways. Zoroark and Zorua nuzzle each other affectionately as the ship approaches a mist-covered island.

sections.heading: Pre-order distribution
sections.text: In Japan, people who pre-ordered tickets to the movie received a Legendary beast; Entei, Raikou or Suicune. In North America, these were distributed at GameStop stores, with a certain amount of time allotted for each of the three Pokémon. They were also later distributed via Wi-Fi for European language games and locally in . The Shiny Legendary beasts allow players to encounter at the Lostlorn Forest when migrated into a Generation V game.

sections.heading: Movie distribution
sections.text: A Celebi could also be downloaded in the cinema when the film was showing in theaters. In addition, Celebi was distributed at GameStop stores at the Pokémon Black and White Sampling Tour and other GameStop stores soon afterward. These Celebi allow players to befriend at Castelia City.

sections.heading: Other distributions
sections.text:
Goone's Scizor was made available to Japanese and Korean versions of the Generation IV games via Wi-Fi.

Those who attended the Black and White Tour in the United States and obtained tickets to the movie could turn in their ticket stubs later on to receive an Pokémon TCG card featuring .

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
This was released between DP183 and DP184 in Japan. However, it chronologically takes place sometime before the aforementioned episodes, as they are placed in the middle of the Lily of the Valley Conference.
This is the only Pokémon the Series: Diamond and Pearl movie that is a standalone movie. The other three Diamond & Pearl movies are part of a trilogy. As such, it is the only Diamond & Pearl movie not to star a member of the Pokémon of myth.
The movie's fictitious setting is based on various locations in and , such as , , , and .
This movie marks the first time all three of the Legendary beasts appear at the same time in the , and also the first time receives a starring role in a movie.
This movie also marks the first time a Legendary Pokémon (in this case, Raikou, Entei, and Suicune) appears in the .
This is the third movie so far that does not have a Legendary Pokémon as the main featured Pokémon, the first being Spell of the Unown: Entei and the second being Lucario and the Mystery of Mew.
This movie ends with Team Rocket being the last characters to appear before the ending credits. This is a pattern found in early movies, which stopped occurring after Celebi: The Voice of the Forest, and has not happened again.
The teaser trailer shown at the end of Arceus and the Jewel of Life showed and locked in an aerial battle, while a later trailer showed a strange city and Ash meeting a darker version of himself. None of these elements made it into the final movie.
This movie was released in Taiwan on July 30, 2010, which was just 20 days after its Japanese premiere.
Professor Rowan, , Johanna, Paul, Zoey, , Nando, , Conway, Ursula, and Palmer make cameo appearances in the movie's credits, along with the Sinnoh Gym Leaders battled and Elite Four. Most of them appear with one of their Pokémon.
makes a cameo in the beginning of the movie with a , seen in with Ash.
This makes this movie the second in which Ash battles a Trainer with a Donphan in the beginning. The first was in Mewtwo Strikes Back.
The Officer Jenny seen in this movie has a star symbol on her hat, which was the same symbol worn by the Jenny in Viridian City (who was also the first Officer Jenny to appear in the animated series).
This is the only animated series appearance of a Generation V Pokémon prior to Pokémon the Series: Black & White.
When Team Rocket sees Zoroark, Jessie asks "Who's that Pokémon?". While this is obviously a reference to the feature of the same name in the TV show, it may also be a premonition that it would return to the show starting with the next season.
During the scene where flies around the city, when it calms the feuding Pokémon, and when it revives Zoroark, remade versions of the Voice of the Forest melody from Celebi: The Voice of the Forest can be heard.
The movie was shown at local theaters during the Pokémon Black Version and White Version Tour between February 5, 2011 and March 20, 2011 in .
This makes it the first movie shown in U.S. theaters since Pokémon Heroes: Latios & Latias in 2003.
In the initial Cartoon Network broadcasts, the entire prologue was cut, with the movie beginning immediately at the title sequence. These scenes are present in the theatrical version.
This cut was made by Cartoon Network The Pokémon Company International's permission, and was restored in future airings as of February 16, 2011.
As of this movie, Ash has seen all the Legendary Pokémon from the first four generations at least once.
Karl's cap has a picture of a on it; that Pokémon had only been officially revealed four days prior to this movie's release.
During the Pokémon Baccer match, the announcer titles Kodai's team as the Nimbasa Legends. Nimbasa City is a city that appears in Generation V, hinting to Kodai's possible origins.
During the title sequence, after Zoroark: Master of Illusions is displayed, a part of the music from Lostlorn Forest can be heard.
This movie marks the debut of the made-up writing system created for the animated series, which would start being used consistently from Pokémon the Series: Black & White onward.
This movie marks the first animated series appearance of a other than the one that belonged to Morrison.

sections.heading: Errors
sections.text:
In the credits, Palmer's 's mouth was the same color as its horn and the top-most part of its body.
As Ash asks "What do you mean?" in the scene when Ash and his friends were trapped in the cage by Kodai, Dawn's hair clip is the same color as her hair.
During Kodai's "apology" broadcast, Peg can be briefly seen standing with Ash and his friends. Her eyes are drawn oval-shaped, with visible pupils, as opposed to all of the other times in the movie when she is drawn without pupils. 
Among the Pokémon using is , a Pokémon unable to legally learn the move.
Whether Zorua's illusions allow it to use the natural abilities of the Pokémon its disguised as is inconsistent. Early in the film, Zorua is able to float down safely from a dangerous height while taking the form of . Despite this, it is shown later in the movie that Zorua cannot fly as .
Near the end of the movie, while Kodai is pursuing and (disguised as Celebi), his illusion canceler failed to reveal Zorua's disguise even though it was not yet broken at that point.
Karl's uses to deflect a from which should not have worked as Psywave is a special move and Reflect only affects physical moves.

sections.heading: Dub edits
sections.text:
Zorua calls Zoroark "Meema" instead of "Maa".
In the original version, the password to Kodai's secret files was "Time Ripple". In the English dub it is "V-I-S-I-O-N". This is likely due to "Time Ripple" having 6 characters in Japanese kana but 11 letters in English.
During the climax of the movie in Japanese, Zorua says "Maa... I couldn't do anything", while in the English dub, he instead says the much darker phrase of "I guess there isn't much time left for me..." implying that he expects to die.
While Zorua is in Tangrowth's arm after being hit by Sleep Powder, he mumbles "I'm not sleepy...!" in Japanese, while in English he remains silent.
Ice Cream Syndrome is replaced as the ending song of the movie by a new song titled I Believe in You.
Zorua was originally told by Zoroark never to talk to humans, but in the dub, was told never to talk to strangers.

Pokémon—Zoroark: Master of Illusions (Japanese: ポケットモンスター　ダイヤモンド＆パール　 の 　ゾロアーク Pocket Monsters Diamond & Pearl the Movie - Supreme Ruler of Illusions: Zoroark) is the fourth and final Pokémon the Series: Diamond and Pearl movie and the thirteenth Pokémon movie overall. It premiered in Japanese theaters on July 10, 2010, and in in select theaters and on on February 5, 2011. In , it premiered on February 26, 2011 on the channel. The premiere was shown on YTV on March 12, 2011. It was released on Blu-ray and DVD in on June 1, 2011, and was released on DVD in the UK on August 29, 2011 and in the US on September 20, 2011. On September 17, 2011 and September 18, 2011, it was available on Pokémon.com.
